title: Renewable Energy Comparisons: Foundations
welcome_lead: Compare solar, wind, hydro and tidal energy by output, cost and impact.
meta_desc: GCSE Environmental Science adventure on renewable energy comparison foundations: solar, wind, hydro, tidal.
final_note: You can now match the right renewable to the right place.

concepts.def: Photovoltaic panels converting sunlight to electricity.
Wind turbines built on land for power generation.
Wind turbines built at sea, with stronger winds.
Using moving water (rivers) to spin turbines.
Power from predictable rise and fall of tides.
Heat from Earth's interior generating power/heat.

walkthroughs.body_html: Solar PV works in daylight and rooftop scale, with UK capacity factor of around 10 to 12 percent due to cloud and short winters. Onshore wind in UK reaches around 30 to 40 percent capacity factor, offshore 40 to 50 percent thanks to stronger steadier winds. Wind needs siting away from homes; solar can scale on existing buildings.

Hydroelectric dams have capacity factors of around 40 to 60 percent and provide flexible storage via pumped hydro. Tidal lagoons and barrages produce predictable output tied to lunar cycles, but only when tides flow. Tidal range schemes need large estuaries (Severn Estuary studied). Both can harm aquatic ecosystems if poorly sited.

Geothermal uses Earth's internal heat. Iceland generates around 25 percent of electricity from geothermal. The UK has limited high-grade resources but ground-source heat pumps work everywhere, transferring stable subsurface heat (around 10 to 12 C in UK soils) into buildings using a small amount of electricity. Capacity factors above 80 percent are typical for geothermal power.
